items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Public Administration, Economics, Healthcare Administration, Research Administration, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Minimum of five years of research administration experience.
Experience supporting sponsored research in a university, healthcare, or academic medical center environment.
Experience managing budgets, financial reporting, forecasting, and financial analysis.
Experience managing complex grant portfolios involving multiple investigators and subawards.
Experience with electronic research administration and proposal management systems.

Our Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behavior is seeking to hire a full-time Research Administrator to join our Semel Central Administration team. The Semel Institute is an internationally recognized center dedicated to advancing research, education, and innovation in neuroscience, mental health, and human behavior. Supporting a diverse portfolio of federally funded, foundation-supported, and industry-sponsored research, the Central Administration team plans a critical role in ensuring the successful financial and administrative management of research programs across the institute.

You will serve as a key partner to faculty investigators and department leadership, providing expert post-award research administration and financial oversight for portfolio of sponsored research awards. You will help ensure compliance with sponsor and university requirements while supporting the financial health and operational success of research programs. Key Responsibilities
Manage the post-award administration of sponsored research projects from award setup through closeout.
Monitor award budgets, expenditures, and financial activity to ensure compliance with sponsor and university guidelines.
Prepare financial reports, reconciliations, budget forecasts, and cost projections.
Coordinate sponsor reporting, funding requests, extensions, and award modifications.
Provide guidance to Principal Investigators and department stakeholders regarding research administration and compliance requirements.
Manage complex awards, including projects involving multiple investigators, subawards, and diverse funding sources.
Analyze financial data, identify issues, and recommend solutions to support effective award management
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.
Knowledge of grant funding processes, sponsored research administration, and compliance requirements.
Knowledge of federal, state, foundation, and industry-sponsored research funding.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational and records management skills.
Ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
Excellent interpersonal skills and attention to detail.
